subject: Mathematics
learning_objectives: Understand addition as the process of putting groups together or combining quantities
Recognize and correctly use the plus sign (+) and equal sign (=)
Perform single-digit and basic two-digit addition with sums up to 20
Solve simple one-step real-world addition word problems
introduction: Start with a relatable storytelling scenario: 'Ravi has 3 bright red marbles in his pocket. His friend Anita gives him 2 more marbles. Let us put all the marbles together and count how many marbles Ravi has in total!' Demonstrate that adding means putting together and finding the total.
teacher_activity: Demonstrate combining physical groups using counting blocks and magnetic counters on the board.
Introduce mathematical symbols: '+' means 'add/plus' and '=' means 'equals/is equal to'.
Write out number sentences clearly (e.g., 3 + 2 = 5) and explain each part.
Guide students through the number line hopping method (start at 3, jump 2 steps right to land on 5).
student_activity: Use fingers and counting sticks to combine two groups of numbers.
Draw dots or tally marks in notebooks to solve addition problems.
Practice jumping along a floor number line to find sums.
Write out mathematical equations neatly on slates or notebooks.

lesson_steps.title: Story Warm-up & Concept Introduction
lesson_steps.description: Tell the marble story and demonstrate physical grouping of items to illustrate addition.

lesson_steps.title: Introducing Symbols (+ and =)
lesson_steps.description: Teach the plus (+) and equals (=) symbols and how to read addition equations aloud.

lesson_steps.title: Guided Examples & Visual Modeling
lesson_steps.description: Work through 4 addition examples on the board using dots, fingers, and the number line.

lesson_steps.title: Interactive Practice & Partner Work
lesson_steps.description: Students work in pairs solving addition cards using counters.

lesson_steps.title: Recap & Quick Quiz
lesson_steps.description: Conduct a quick-fire verbal addition game to reinforce learning.

examples.explanation: 2 dots plus 3 dots equals 5 dots altogether.
4 stars and 4 more stars give a total of 8 stars.
Adding 1 to any number gives the very next number: 6 + 1 = 7.
Adding 0 to any number keeps the number the same: 5 + 0 = 5.

classroom_activities.description: Students roll two dice, write down the two numbers, and add them together to get the total.
A student stands on the starting number on a floor mat and takes forward steps equal to the second number to land on the answer.

assessment_questions.question: If you have 5 candies and get 2 more, how many candies do you have in total?

homework.title: Addition Explorer Worksheet
tasks: Solve the following 5 sums in your notebook: 3 + 3, 5 + 4, 7 + 1, 2 + 6, 4 + 5.
Draw 3 circles, then draw 4 triangles. Count all shapes together and write the total number.
Create one addition story at home with fruits or books and share it tomorrow.
